Danso had made it clear he wanted to leave Tottenham this summer in search of regular first-team football.

Eintracht Frankfurt are in talks with Nottingham Forest over another loan move for forward Arnaud Kalimuendo.

Frankfurt signed the Frenchman on loan in January and are negotiating a return for Forest’s £26m signing from Rennes.

Oliver Glasner, Forest’s head coach, had been intent on keeping Kalimuendo but it is understood Frankfurt’s strong interest has altered the club’s thinking.

Morato, the centre-back, is expected to join West Ham United on loan.

Forest are exploring potential signings but are determined to stay calm and only pursue deals that make financial sense. A winger and a No 6 are the two priority targets if there are deals to be done.

On Tuesday evening, the Tottenham and Brazil forward posted an emotional message on Instagram amid reports of a possible move back to Everton.

He wrote: “After everything I’ve been through in recent years, I decided that never again would others decide my future for me.

“I went through a lot of bad things during this time, and almost all of them happened because of decisions made by other people. Pressure, threats, retaliation – none of that scares me. I’ve been through worse, believe me!

“I have always made it clear at every opportunity that my departure to another place would also have to be good for the club. If it wasn’t, I would never accept it... just as I didn’t accept it when everything here was falling apart and they needed me.”

Richarlison added: “I stayed and gave my all. So, I hope they treat my situation with the same respect that I have always had for Spurs and for all the people who worked with me during this period. Just don’t try to decide for me.”

“If Spurs and Everton reach an agreement, I will return to the club of my heart. My intention was indeed to go back to the place where I was very happy.

“But negotiations were being done the way other people wanted, and it won’t be that way anymore. Despite all this turmoil, I have a contract with Spurs and I will remain at the club’s disposal.”

It will be good news for Arsenal if Folarin Balogun completes his £40m move to Everton today. When Arsenal sold Balogun to Monaco in 2023, they negotiated a sell-on clause of 17.5 per cent. According to my maths, that means Arsenal will get £7m from this transfer. Not to be sniffed at!

Hull City are close to agreeing a fee of around £7.5m for Stoke City winger Sorba Thomas.

The Wales international has been a long-term target for Hull and negotiations are now approaching a conclusion.

Thomas has been pushing a move through and is expected to leave Stoke after one full season.

As has become the norm this summer Acun Ilicali has posted a cryptic message on X, which has prompted speculation among Hull City fans. The club has been linked with Everton holding midfielder Tim Iroegbunam.

What a couple of weeks it has been for Robert Sanchez. He came into this season as Chelsea’s No 1, but after a difficult start to the campaign and Emi Martinez’s arrival, reports suggest he could be moving away from Stamford Bridge on loan. Cesc Fabregas’s Como appears the probable destination.

Trevoh Chalobah, who left Chelsea for Como last month, has taken to his “secondary” Instagram account to post the following picture...

Meanwhile, as reported by Telegraph Sport yesterday, striker flop Nick Woltemade is moving to Juventus on a season-long loan. The club’s record signing from as year ago at £64m is moving to Turin for a £3.5m loan fee with the Serie A squad covering the full cost of his wages.

Newcastle will complete the £51m signing of forward Matias Fernandez-Pardo from Lille today but that is expected to be it in terms of incomings.

The Belgium international will become the club’s eighth signing of the summer and his versatility – he can play as a centre forward, a No 10 or out wide – means there are no more gaps to fill in the squad.

In an ideal world, Newcastle would have liked to sign another defender but none of their targets were still on the market. With Dan Burn due to return from injury in a few weeks, they have four centre-backs while new arrival Amar Dedic can play on both sides as a full-back.

In terms of outgoings, Joe Willock and Jacob Murphy are expected to stay at the club despite interest from Nottingham Forest and Besiktas. Young striker Sean Neave will be allowed to leave on loan. The 19-year-old has offers from clubs in the Championship and League One but Newcastle want him to go somewhere he has the best chance of getting regular first-team football.

City have been this summer’s selling kings and have had six players leave the club in deals worth more than £45m. Compare that to the summer when Pep Guardiola first arrived at the club, in 2016, when City generated just £23m from sales and made losses on Edin Dzeko and Stevan Jovetic, while Martín Demichelis departed on a free transfer.

Fast forward to this summer and more than £300m worth of players have been sold, with a further £60m arriving at the end of the season when Omar Marmoush’s loan to Tottenham Hotspur becomes permanent.

Given how Jaissle wants Newcastle to play, it is plain to see why Fernandez-Pardo appeals to him. Quick, direct and only 21 – he would surely fit right in at St James’ Park.

The Leeds wide man has a medical booked with Fiorentina today. He made a handful of appearances for Daniel Farke’s side during pre-season but has not featured since the start of the 2026-27 campaign.

✈️ L'arrivo di Gnonto a Firenze ⚜️ pic.twitter.com/nEFngsyxQP

Very unlikely that Liverpool will be doing any major incoming business but there may yet be some departures. Jayden Danns, who broke through three years ago and played in the 2024 League Cup final defeat of Chelsea, is attracting interest from clubs in Europe, who want to take him on loan. Danns, a promising striker, has had injury issues and is working his way back to full fitness but his long-term ambition is to prove to Andoni Iraola that he can be part of his squad.

Fax machines are whirring as the clock continues to tick towards the transfer deadline, but who does your club need to sign? Let us know in the comments below!

Aston Villa are to confirm the signings of £50m winger Ibrahim Mbaye and £25m centre-back Taylor Harwood-Bellis this morning.

Mbaye and Harwood-Bellis takes the number of Villa’s signings this summer to 10, with Unai Emery ruling out any more additions after the 1-0 defeat by Arsenal last night.

Emery also disclosed that forward Tammy Abraham will be staying at Villa Park, amid interest from Ipswich Town.

The one player who could leave today is Jamaica international Leon Bailey, who has interest from clubs in Europe, and Hull City.

Nottingham Forest can confirm Omari Hutchinson has joined AC Milan on a season-long loan deal, with the Italian club holding an option to make the transfer permanent.Everyone at Nottingham Forest wishes Omari all the best for his time in Italy. pic.twitter.com/fSv1uNGh2Y

Fulham remain locked in discussions with Rayo Vallecano to agree a fee for right-back Andrei Ratiu, with the Romania international having confirmed he wants to join Alvaro Arbeloa’s side. The spin-off with this deal is that it will accelerate Kenny Tete’s switch to Everton, for a fee in the region of £9.5m.

On the subject of right-backs, Nathan Patterson, who has had a difficult time at Everton, has been granted permission to travel to Italy to undergo a medical with Torino.

Matias Fernandez-Pardo is on the verge of joining Newcastle United, and Luke Edwards reported that the forward’s arrival is likely to pave the way for Nick Woltemade’s departure.

The German enjoyed a fruitful start to life in England after signing last summer, scoring seven Premier League goals before the turn of the year, but could only manage one goal in the second half of the season. While Eddie Howe experimented with Woltemade in a more withdrawn No 10 role, there was a clear drop-off in his game-time after Christmas.

Newcastle are ready to pay around £51m to sign Fernandez-Pardo after holding face-to-face talks with Lille last week. The 21-year-old is a versatile attacker and Newcastle identified him as a top target months ago. If they can complete a deal, it could speed up the departure of Nick Woltemade, who is wanted by Juventus.

The Brazilian has asked to leave Spurs and has been linked to a move back to Everton. However, his hopes of returning to Merseyside may have taken a hit on Monday night, when Everton agreed a £40m deal with Monaco for striker Folarin Balogun.

Brighton are keen to sign Azeez from Millwall and have made multiple offers for the forward. Millwall want at least £15m for Azeez, who scored 11 goals in the Championship last season. Ipswich Town have previously shown interest in Azeez.

Leeds are signing Melvin Bard on loan from Nice. One-season deal for the 25-year-old who will compete for a place in the first-team under Daniel Farke.

We’re expecting four departures from Arsenal today. Nwaneri to Dortmund on loan (see my colleague Mike McGrath’s post below), Gabriel Martinelli to Al-Hilal, Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Fabio Vieira to Hamburg. Those deals should raise around £70m.

Will there be any incomings? The Julian Alvarez situation seems unlikely to develop in Arsenal’s favour, barring a dramatic change of heart. As reported by Telegraph Sport yesterday, Lyon winger Malick Fofana is a potential option.

Borussia Dortmund have been trying to close out a loan deal for Arsenal winger Ethan Nwaneri, as reported by Telegraph Sport yesterday. The German club have previously attempted to land the 19-year-old and this time want him on a deal for the season.

It is expected to be another busy deadline day in the Premier League, with many clubs still hoping to finalise deals before the transfer window shuts at 11pm. Here, Telegraph Sport identifies 10 potential high-profile moves that could yet go through.

This has been the most dramatic and relentless saga of the European transfer window. The situation, as far as we understand it, is as follows: Barcelona want Alvarez and Alvarez wants Barcelona, but Atletico Madrid refuse to sell him to Barcelona. Arsenal want Alvarez, and Atletico are more open to selling him to Arsenal, but Alvarez only wants Barcelona. For a move to happen, it will require one party to change their mind. Either Atletico decides to sell to Barcelona, or Alvarez decides he will join Arsenal.

Another long-running saga. Chelsea are well aware of City’s interest in Fernandez but want a massive fee for the Argentina international, having initially valued him at £120m. City have the cash and the space in the squad after saying goodbye to Rodri, Tijani Reijnders, Nico Gonzalez and Bernardo Silva this summer. Fernandez has not featured in Chelsea’s last two games.

As reported by Telegraph Sport last week, Chelsea have identified Monaco midfielder Camara as a target amid the uncertainty over Fernandez’s future. French reports on Monday suggested the move may have stalled, however. The clock is ticking.

Spurs had been working on a deal to sign Ndiaye from Everton but they now appear to have fallen behind City in the race for the winger, as a consequence of City failing in their attempt to sign Cody Gakpo from Liverpool. City are ready to complete the hijack on deadline day.

A deal that, as of Monday night, is regarded as unlikely to happen. As with their interest in Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh, Liverpool have so far been unable to strike a deal with Crystal Palace for Sarr, who scored 21 goals in 45 games last season. Liverpool would only allow Gakpo to leave if a replacement, such as Sarr, can be signed.

Burnley are one of a host of Championship clubs who are interested in the young Manchester United left-back Harry Amass. There have been talks over a potential permanent deal but a loan cannot be ruled out. The 19-year-old joined United from Watford in 2023.

Everton have reached an agreement with Manchester City to sign Jack Grealish on another season long loan. It has been a very busy summer of outgoings at City and Grealish will be the latest to depart as he prepares to return to Merseyside. He started well at Everton last season before injury in January derailed his campaign.

A big year ahead for the English midfielder.

Tottenham are set to complete a double deal for Chelsea pair Mykhailo Mudryk and Tosin Adarabioyo after missing out on Iliman Ndiaye.

Spurs will take Mudryk on loan for the season having seen their attempt to land Ndiaye fail when Manchester City agreed a £65m deal with Everton.

Mudryk, 25, worked with Spurs head coach Roberto De Zerbi at Shakthtar Donetsk, in the winger’s homeland Ukraine, before his £85m move to Chelsea in 2023.

Leeds United had shown interest but instead he will be reunited with De Zerbi, effectively taking Ndiaye’s place as a wide-forward option.

Adarabioyo will be a permanent deal to Spurs as they are not allowed to loan two players from a Premier League club.

Good morning and welcome to live coverage of transfer deadline day. We are deep into stoppage time in this summer window and we will bring you the key developments as teams scramble to get last-minute deals over the line before the full-time whistle blows at 11pm.

Enzo Fernández remains a City target, and his omission from Xabi Alonso’s match-day squad against Brighton and Hove Albion on Sunday has only added weight to the feeling that he might reunite with former Chelsea head coach Enzo Maresca. City would be required to meet the Londoners’ £120m asking price, which is just shy of Alexander Isak’s £125m British record fee.

Meanwhile, Julián Alvarez’s situation at Atlético Madrid continues to be monitored by Arsenal. The Argentina forward’s dream move to Barcelona appears a no-goer as Atlético remain steadfast in their refusal to sell to their La Liga rivals. While this could bring Arsenal into the picture, it is understood that Alvarez – who missed three training sessions last week and did not travel to Sevilla with Diego Simeone’s squad on Saturday – is not pursuing a return to England.

A Mohamed Salah-shaped hole on Liverpool’s right flank has been filled by Bradley Barcola after the club agreed a £123m deal with Paris St-Germain. His signing looked as though it might trigger Cody Gakpo’s move away from Anfield as the winger had been linked with a move to Manchester City, but it appears that the Netherlands international will stay put. Maresca’s side have instead hijacked Spurs’ move for Iliman Ndiaye, and the north London outfit pivoted to take Myhailo Mudryk and Tosin Adarabioyo from Chelsea, on loan and permanent deals respectively. Liverpool could yet swoop for Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh or Ismaïla Sarr.

Newcastle United appeared to have reached their nadir this summer after Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimarães and Eddie Howe departed, but Matthias Jaissle has breathed life into St James’ Park by delivering an exciting brand of football that leans on the team’s explosive pace in forward positions. Lille’s Matias Fernandez-Pardo would fit this system and is on the brink of joining Newcastle in a deal worth £51m, which could signal Nick Woltemade’s exit.

Barcola is the window’s most expensive acquisition, followed by Morgan Rogers who was prised away from Aston Villa to the tune of £118m, and has already hit the ground running for the Londoners. He cost £2m more than his England team-mate Elliot Anderson, who swapped Nottingham Forest for Manchester City. Elite midfielders have proved a gilded commodity with seven of the Premier League’s top 10 most expensive acquisitions coming in the middle of the park. The departures of Rodri, Casemiro and others will have played their part.

Praying for a deadline-day saviour or counting down the seconds until the window slams shut on directors of football hoping to lure away your club’s next big thing? Let us know in the comments and join the conversation as the day unfolds.

#1855. Arsenal transfer news: Gunners 'monitoring' exciting £20m former Tottenham striker

By Saikat Mandal | 14 Nov 2026 17:25

Arsenal are reportedly showing an interest in former Tottenham Hotspur striker Will Lankshear, who has been in outstanding form this season.

The 20-year-old joined Middlesbrough from Spurs during the summer transfer window for a fee of £20m and has established himself as one of the Championship's most exciting young strikers.

Lankshear has scored 15 goals in 16 appearances for the Teesside club and currently leads the Championship scoring charts.

The youngster has played a major role in Boro's impressive campaign, helping them climb to second in the Championship table, level on points with leaders Birmingham City.

A host of clubs, including Leeds United, were interested in signing Lankshear during the summer window, but Boro won the race for his signature, a decision that has paid dividends so far.

According to a report from TeamTalk, several Premier League clubs have watched Lankshear in action this season, with his remarkable goalscoring form attracting plenty of attention.

The report claims that Premier League champions Arsenal, Lankshear's first club as a youngster, are monitoring his situation, while Tottenham and Manchester United are also interested.

Tottenham reportedly secured a matching-right option when allowing Lankshear to join Middlesbrough, but did not include a buy-back clause in the agreement.

Newcastle United, Sunderland and Leeds are also keeping tabs on the striker, while German giants Borussia Dortmund have been monitoring his development.

The Gunners failed to sign a new striker during the summer despite being heavily linked with several attacking targets, including Atletico Madrid's Julian Alvarez.

Viktor Gyokeres has managed just one Premier League start this season and is yet to find the net in seven appearances.

Instead, Kai Havertz has been deployed predominantly as the central striker, with the Germany international scoring three Premier League goals in 10 appearances so far.

Lankshear is reportedly enjoying life at the Riverside Stadium, and Middlesbrough have no plans to offload him in January, making a mid-season departure highly unlikely.

#1854. A captain’s performance and unlucky to concede three – Maignan and Rabiot’s rating vs. Italy

Last night, Mike Maignan and Adrien Rabiot were opponents at San Siro, a rare occasion for the star AC Milan duo.

Before last night’s game, there was plenty of attention given to Maignan and the shared story he had with Gianluigi Donnarumma. For both, it was a return home, but only the Frenchman (or duo) were given a warm welcome from the Rossoneri in the crowd.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

How did they perform in their home stadium, though?

As Gazzetta dello Sport – seen below – writes, Maignan’s performance was worthy of a 6/10. However, there were frustrations with some of his decisions to rush out, leading to questions about the need for him to be a ‘goalkeeper-superhero’.

For Rabiot, it was a 5.5 for his performance. The Frenchman struggled to find space when attacking, and whilst France’s attack was strong, they were missing some key names.

Elsewhere, Goal gave Maignan a 6/10 thanks to some good stops against Pio Esposito and admitted that he couldn’t have done much with either of his goals. Additionally, he dove the right way for the penalty, but power took it past him.

Rabiot, though, was bumped up to a 7/10. The captain ‘set the tone’ at both ends and was unlucky not to score at least once. Not only that, but he made an excellent recovery run to stop Riccardo Calafiori, which showed how important he is in the midfield.

#1853. Liverpool transfer news: Reds to 'hold talks' over loanee return in January

By Saikat Mandal | 14 Nov 2026 17:56

Liverpool are reportedly set to hold talks with Valencia over a potential early return for Harvey Elliott in the January transfer window.

Elliott joined Los Che on loan from Liverpool during the summer window, but he has made just six substitute appearances in La Liga, accumulating only 152 minutes of action.

The 23-year-old spent last season on loan at Aston Villa, which also proved to be a frustrating experience for him.

After failing to impress Andoni Iraola sufficiently during pre-season, many believed that a move to Spain could help rejuvenate his career, but that has not been the case.

There were reports that Valencia had placed Elliott on a special fitness regime after he arrived at the club overweight, but it appears that they may already be losing patience with him.

According to Las Provincias (via Sport Witness), Valencia could be looking to terminate his loan spell early, with talks potentially taking place over sending him back to Anfield.

Aside from concerns over his weight, Valencia are also reportedly unhappy with his lack of professionalism.

Elliott was sent off during the clash against Villarreal and subsequently issued an apology to his teammates.

Time appears to be running out for the midfielder, and unless he shows significant improvement in the coming weeks, an early return to Liverpool could be firmly on the cards.

Elliott is under contract at Liverpool until 2028, but the chances of him reviving his career at Anfield appear slim.

Even if he returns in January, which would arguably bolster Liverpool's attacking options, there are doubts over whether Iraola would give him regular opportunities given the number of alternatives now at his disposal.

Liverpool have four versatile wide players in Bradley Barcola, Victor Munoz, Rio Ngumoha and Cody Gakpo, leaving Elliott facing an uphill battle to force his way into the side.

There is also considerable competition for the number 10 role, meaning Liverpool would most likely look to send him out on another loan even if he returns in January.

#1852. GdS: A midfielder with a handbrake – Sylla’s journey to USG and why Milan are interested

AC Milan have been considering a move for Massire Sylla recently and the Senegalese defender’s stock is only rising currently.

There are plenty of defensive options for Milan in the winter mercato. Goncalo Inacio is probably the preference for most, but the profile of Sylla cannot be ignored. Another signing for the future, he’s similar in many ways to Sankhoun Diawara, and the Frenchman has already started to have an impact.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Gazzetta dello Sport have looked a little at his background and his profile. A physical defender, he has previously admitted that he’s a lover of ‘the fight’; a player who loves duels and wins them a lot of the time.

Called up to the Senegalese national team this month, his story is one of patience, tenacity and the ability to persist when faced with obstacles. His career started at Diambars Academy, one of the most notorious in Senegal, starting as a midfielder but eventually moving back to defence.

His coaches wanted him to learn to play with his feet, but his defensive qualities shone, hence the move back. With that, though, he started to see the ball more and both aspects of his game improved substantially.

From there, he joined Pau in 2024 and within six months, he was playing for the senior team in Ligue 2. At 19, he moved to Lyn and then Union Saint-Gilloise paid €2 million for him last January.

It wasn’t an immediate fit, though, and he was called overexcited, thanks to his yellow card record. Yet, he’s settled and now is a key figure in a three-man defence and picking out his best traits are difficult because there are so many.

#1849. John McGinn tells Scotland fans where to place Kool-Aid frustrations amid ‘March or September’ warning

Scotland may have got the win they needed against North Macedonia on Friday night; however, the grumble of discontent which greeted the final whistle proved that supporters are not yet ready to drink the Sebastien Pocognoli Kool-Aid.

Rescued by two second-half goals from John McGinn, the Aston Villa skipper spared his side’s blushes as they ran out 2-1 winners to keep alive their slim hopes of qualifying for the Nations League playoffs. Their overall performance was perhaps best described as patchy, though.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Booed off the park by sections of the home crowd at the break, McGinn admits he takes no issue with the Tartan Army voicing their displeasure at the team’s on-pitch displays, but has pleaded with them to vent their ire at himself and the more experienced names in Scotland’s dressing room than the fresh faces as they look to adjust to Pocognoli’s methods.

Get our daily football newsletter by clicking here.

“The manager's got a great reputation and a good record at both places he's went,” said McGinn following his two goal haul. “The most important thing now in football is individuals don't win you games. It's unity, teamwork and everyone on the same page. And you see how successful clubs do it, successful countries and we want to be one of them. It's not going to happen overnight.

“There's a lot to learn but we did create big chances in the game where we could have scored three, four or five and it could be a different story. This isn't something that gets fixed in March or even next September. it will start to build over the next 18 months. I think the young players are starting to show now more. Luke Graham tonight, I thought he was brilliant, it's not easy playing in the middle of a back three.

“He's been waiting for his chance and the manager's shown that if you deserve your chance you're going to get put in there. So we need players like Luke, Porto [Ryan Porteous] coming back, Doaky [Ben Gannon-Doak] showed glimpses tonight. So we've got so many players that can step up and they will. We just need to show that belief and take it to pitch.”

Asked if he felt the fans need to show patience, McGinn said: “Maybe a bit. I understand it's frustrating; it's freezing, you want to see four, five, six goals, but the balance has got to be there. They're entitled to their opinion, but there's got to be a mixture of patience. But at the same time, the supporters are entitled to say whatever they like. But just as long as they hurl anything they want to shout at the experienced boys. Just let the young ones flourish and try to settle into the team.”

Awarded player of the match against North Macedonia, the 31-year-old’s brace shot himself into joint-third in Scotland’s record goalscorers list. McGinn’s international goal tally is now 24, drawing level with Hughie Gallacher, six short of Kenny Dalglish and Denis Law. Asked if it had sunk in yet, the former Hibs man kept his focus on the team, insisting Monday’s clash against Switzerland holds more importance as they look to give themselves a chance of qualifying for the Nations League playoffs.

“A bit strange obviously but at the minute that's gone to the back burner,” said McGinn. “We need to play slightly better. We know that but we're going through a period which I've been used to at club level, a lot of changes, a lot of detail that we need to try and remember and get used to. It's about sticking at it. We're keen to play a style of football that's not easy but it's going to get bums off seats.

“It takes time, over a few years now at club level it's been the exact same for us but the supporters stuck with us, the players stuck at it and it's important that everyone believes in it because if one person drops off or doesn't believe in it that's when it all starts to fall apart. We've got an important win but there's definitely a lot of room for improvement.

“It’s difficult, I know they [Switzerland] drew [vs Slovenia] but they've got a couple of players back that they were missing last time. We want to be competing against these teams away from home, playing the same way. We're going to stick at it, it's not going to be perfect for a while but on Monday night we're no different.”

#1847. Arsenal: Declan Rice drops huge eight-word update on record-breaking contract

By Ben Knapton | 14 Nov 2026 20:11, Last updated: 14 Nov 2026 20:11

Arsenal midfielder Declan Rice has publicly confirmed that he is set to sign a new contract with the Premier League champions.

The former West Ham United captain remains on the same terms he penned upon his arrival in 2023, and he is currently due to become a free agent in the summer of 2028.

However, the Gunners have made tying their engine room lynchpin down to an improved contract a priority, and Mikel Arteta hinted earlier this month that Rice was close to extending.

Fabrizio Romano also reported in October that Arsenal and Rice had made progress in talks over a renewal offer, and it is seemingly just a matter of time before the announcement is made.

Speaking to reporters ahead of Sunday's UEFA Nations League fixture between Spain and England, Rice dropped a major eight-word update, saying: "A new contract will hopefully be arriving soon."

Rice is currently on a £260,000 weekly salary at the Emirates, according to Capology, but his new deal is expected to bump his pay up to a record £350,000 per week.

The England international would therefore become the highest-paid player in the Arsenal squad, ahead of Bukayo Saka, who is believed to be earning £300,000 per week.

Rice's bumper renewal will be just reward for the 27-year-old's seismic impact since joining in a £105m transfer, having registered 58 goal involvements in 173 Arsenal appearances.

Rice has scored 22 goals of his own while setting up 36 more in a red and white kit, and he started 35 Premier League matches during Arsenal's run to title glory last season.

The Englishman has scored one goal and set up five more in 15 matches in all tournaments this season, and he is set to make his 82nd England appearance in Sunday's clash with Spain, where a win will see the Three Lions through to the Nations League quarter-finals as group winners.

Rice is one of nine Arsenal players whose contracts expire at the end of the 2027-28 season, but not every member of that list will be in line for a renewal.

The long-term futures of Kepa Arrizabalaga, Illan Meslier and Mikel Merino are clouded in some uncertainty, and the same goes for the injury-plagued Ben White and Kai Havertz.

However, defensive stalwart Jurrien Timber - who recently delivered a Netherlands "masterclass" - is expected to be a top priority for a new deal in due course, in addition to number one David Raya.

Captain Martin Odegaard could also leave for nothing in 2028, and he recently delivered an update on his Arsenal contract situation.

#1845. Sebastien Pocognoli believes Scotland ‘click’ is coming for player who served up a curate’s egg at Hampden

After 12 games so far, from Liverpool to Ljubljana, from Miami to North Macedonia, the ‘No Scotland, no party’ world tour of 2026 grinds into St Gallen on Monday for one final performance.

What a 12 months it’s been. Scotland at least managed to avoid going a whole calendar year without winning a competitive game at Hampden by narrowly overcoming North Macedonia in the Nations League on Friday night.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

It’s a small triumph considering Scotland were hoping to make history a few months ago by qualifying for the second stage of a major tournament for the first time. So this is where we are, which is where exactly? Wrestling with a system that looks increasingly unsuited to Scotland. Rather than freeing them up, which was Sebastien Pocognoli’s manifesto when he took over, his preferred 3-4-1-2 formation seems to have put the players in a straitjacket. The idea was to play ten yards further forward. Instead, Scotland appear to be going backwards in every sense.

They nevertheless have the chance to end the international year with a truly eye-popping result if they can beat Switzerland, already confirmed as Group B1 winners. It is the 13th match in a year where Scotland have played teams from five of the six FIFA confederations. Six of the matches, including Monday, have been against teams in the top 20 of the Fifa rankings. This perhaps explains the unexceptional total of just five wins, two of them friendlies.

Scotland need another victory on Monday and must hope Slovenia don’t take three points their trip to North Macedonia to finish in the top two and earn a promotion chance via the play-offs this Spring. It’s been a challenging as well as often very memorable year.

The danger is Scotland are already all played out, no one more so than Andy Robertson. No one except Kenny Dalglish has appeared as many times for Scotland as the skipper. Robertson has survived the risk of suspension and will become Scotland’s most capped ever player when, fitness permitting, he lines up on Monday.

Ryan Christie came on for his 75th cap on Friday, while Kieran Tierney, if selected, will earn cap No. 60 against Switzerland. Scott McTominay, meanwhile, will hit the 75-mark.

No one’s getting any younger. But Pocognoli seems determined to keep faith with a system that demands dynamism.

“I think we need to rest well,” he said. “That is the first thing. If we want to play like this we need energy. I will need to consider the best approach for the game regarding the quality and also the fitness of some players. We have some players in the squad who we have to manage. They cannot play two games in a row.”

Aaron Hickey might be one of those, hence him being named among the substitutes for the supposedly less testing fixture against North Macedonia. If he comes back into the side against Switzerland what does that mean for Ben Gannon-Doak? The winger featured at right wing-back and once again produced a curate’s egg of a performance. Good in parts, including when he won Scotland’s match-winning penalty (although even that was after he had taken a poor touch).

The focus and indeed expectation placed on him seems completely unreasonable, although he possibly hasn’t helped himself. It’s what happens when you are named man of the match for Bournemouth in a 3-0 Europa League win over AC Milan.

But this does not mean there's been an overnight cure for the imperfections that dog the player, understandably so given he’s only just turned 21. Pocognoli believes things will “click” for him in time. The right choice will suddenly become his instinctive reaction. The final ball will become a weapon rather than his Achilles heel. “We know that he needs to improve on the end product,” said Pocognoli. “But he created a penalty and against Slovenia and North Macedonia away he created a number of unbelievable one v ones. He did that (on Friday) as well.

“I believe in one moment he will have a click about decision making. I believe if he is playing every game he can make (better) decisions….. he knows that he only has to play a game every two weeks sometimes he can (over)think, ‘This is my moment.’ It is a process. He will become older and will at some point become relaxed in his decision making.”

Whether Gannon-Doak ever achieves his potential might hinge on playing where he ought to be playing, which is as an out-and-out winger. At present, Pocognoli’s preferred formation won’t accommodate this. It’s unlikely that the Belgian is going to change his ways ahead of Monday, when Scotland might really need three centre halves (even if one of them is really a full back).

Former Dundee defender Luke Graham’s assured performance aged just 22 surely means he will line up once more in the middle of defence.

“I have really scanned the quality of the squad and I believe we have the quality to play like this,” said Pocognoli. “I believe that Luke Graham can be important to the defence. “I believe Kieran Tierney can be good in that position. I believe that Ryan Porteous is helpful for how we want to play because he is on the front foot."

Pocognoli mentioned his adherence to a midfield 'box', where Billy Gilmour and Lewis Ferguson act as pivots. “We need speed if we want to use the box,” he said. “We have that with Ben, but we don’t have that unlimited specific quality.

“It is up to me to find the best way to play,” he added. “But it is not easy to bring players who come from different clubs with a different approach to fit into (the system) in two days. But we have a lot of players who play that way in Italy and other places. It has helped me a lot in the past.”

The past is history. Never mind Gannon-Doak, things need to start clicking sooner rather than later for Pocognoli.

#1844. Alexander Isak starts to justify £125m price tag with double

There was a centre-forward who played for Newcastle a couple of years ago. Do you remember him? He was as quick as greased lightning, played on his instincts, had a shot like cannon and could come up with a finish for every situation.

Everyone wanted him, but Liverpool signed him for £125m in August 2025. His name was Alexander Isak but shortly after arriving on Merseyside, it was like he went missing, as the guy who played in red last season bore only a physical resemblance to the guy who had played in black-and-white.

If you had wondered what had happened to him, he reappeared at Portman Road. They say good things come to those who wait. Although nobody at Liverpool would have expected such a delay to see the real Isak, there were no complaints that his career at the club has finally taken off.

Taking the headlines from Bradley Barcola on a big night at Portman Road was going to take some doing, but Isak did just that with a double salvo in the opening nine minutes, a flurry so potent it was like a boxer charging out of their corner and seeing the first blows land flush on their opponent’s jaw.

Poor Ipswich. There is universal recognition that Liverpool are a team – and a club – in transition but they had four players in Isak, Florian Wirtz, Cody Gakpo and Victor Muñoz who had the potential to dismantle the hosts if they clicked and that is precisely what happened.

“With Alex, it is clear,” said Andoni Iraola. “If he is fit, if he is available, if he is in a good shape, he will produce the numbers. My demand with Alex will not be about the goals. It will be about other things so we can play well. And if we play well, we are in good positions. Then goals will come.”

So for all the noisy backing they received from the stands and for all the effort Gary O’Neil’s side put into a contest that TV companies had chosen to broadcast because there was a potential for drama, Isak blew a hole in Ipswich’s hull in the sixth minute and they were submerging from there on in.

A blistering finish from Alexander Isak! 💥 pic.twitter.com/jSGlIZsQtA

How Isak, who had scored against Nottingham Forest last weekend, needed a night like this when he made a genuine difference. But the same was true, too, for Iraola. We live in an era where someone has to be in the eye of a storm and the Basque will know what comes with his new territory.

It had clearly irritated Iraola that Liverpool had gone behind four times in their opening two fixtures and during his pre-match media briefing, he effectively gave a sermon at one point on how slow starts, or giving the opposition a helping hand, would no longer be tolerated.

Quietly, Iraola is making his presence felt. The task he faces is significantly different than the one O’Neil is accomplishing – keeping Ipswich in the division against the odds – but Liverpool’s head coach is a man who knows his own mind and is not afraid to make decisions.

He had responded to criticism of his midfield at Newcastle on the opening weekend by dropping Ryan Gravenberch for the fixture with Forest and his response to scrutiny about his right-back seven days ago was to drop Jeremie Frimpong and bring in Ronald Araújo.

Iraola certainly picked the right team: Araújo, the loan capture from Barcelona, added stature to the back four and there was harmony in how they moved. The Uruguayan’s first instinct was to stay back and Liverpool looked better for it, even if O’Neil, incredibly, felt Ipswich had the better of things.

Emersonn, Ipswich’s Brazilian striker, did not see the ball in the opening exchanges and, by the time he did, Liverpool had zoomed into the distance to such an extent that you felt it was going to be impossible for them to peg their visitors back.

“I hate having to talk about good performances when you do not get points,” O’Neil declared to a room full of raised eyebrows and you can only assume his message was to ensure that morale in the dressing room was not drooping.

What damage was inflicted with Liverpool’s first significant attack. Gakpo, the subject of an £80m bid from Manchester City, was never going to allow transfer speculation to disrupt his focus and he nudged a perfect little ball into Isak’s path in the sixth minute to show his wellbeing.

The next move announced the return of Isak. One touch gave him an avenue to shoot, the next was a shot with his right foot that was so hard from 16 yards, on an angle, it bent the wrists of Kjell Scherpen as it howled into the net. Critics will feel Ipswich’s keeper should have done better.

Your first thought was to think of the first goal Isak scored in English football in September 2022, a similarly venomous drive, against Liverpool at Anfield. He oozed quality that evening, his pace and skill had Jürgen Klopp’s defenders persistently fretting and this is what he was doing again.

It was no coincidence that three minutes later, he came up with another wonderful goal. This one owed much to the beautiful pass Gakpo presented to him, an inch-perfect through ball with the outside of his right foot, but Isak still showed great poise to bamboozle Scherpen.

Inside NINE minutes Alexander Isak has two goals! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/3UGq0bwqRm

“He owes me a few assists now!” chirped the selfless Gakpo.

A hat-trick could have arrived in the 32nd minute but Isak was a kneecap offside as he dispatched a pass from Wirtz and, perhaps, he will have been disappointed to have made way on the hour having not secured the match ball for his efforts.

Liverpool, too, will be frustrated that they did not made sure of three points before the time Isak made way for Barcola – what Alexis Mac Alliser was thinking when he fluffed an unmarked header from six yards, only he will know – but it was not a night to nitpick.

There will be easier assignments on the horizon for Ipswich, even though O’Neil insisted they more than held their own against world-class opponents. And you can say for sure there will be more goals and wins for Liverpool and Isak if they continue in this encouraging manner.

“I witnessed what a great coach he was at Bournemouth. He is not the sort of manager you are going to see making clever patterns in his box. He just does not see the risk. He will want to get the ball to the players who want to make a difference. Coaches do not show how good they are by how they play out from the back. The important thing is when you get it in the final third, you make things happen. That is what he will want to improve. He will want Alexander Isak when he has not got the ball to press. He will want the same of Florian Wirtz. The difficulty will come with Champions League football and not putting too many demands on his players. If he gets it right, he has got a wonderful squad to work with.”

"My demands will not be about the goals, my fights with him are about other stuff." Andoni Iraola speaking about Alexander Isak 🔊 pic.twitter.com/B4zUG2IGfS

“He has had good minutes, a good pass in a counter, a good couple of chances when he was going against the goalkeeper and we have not found him. We need to learn these movements because he will be there threatening in behind all the team. But he looks confident on the ball as always. He had not played any competitive minutes since the World Cup so we had to be a little bit more careful.”

"Yeah, that's nice" 😁Alexander Isak talks through his second goal vs Ipswich 🔍 pic.twitter.com/diG2xv50Bw

“We were waiting for the first win, and we were talking about starting the game well, which we have not done recently. And we did that with two goals. With a normal pre-season, I think we are starting to get the way we want to play, being offensive and attack the defence. We showed that today. We scored two and could have scored more.

“It was not easy. It was a long injury, a difficult season [last season] in general. I was thinking; I want to have a good World Cup firstly and then to start the season well, which I feel like I have done now. That season is kind of behind me, but it was not easy.”

The final whistle goes at Portman Road and Andoni Iraola picks up his first win as Liverpool boss with a 2-0 victory thanks to Isak’s quickfire double inside the opening 10 minutes. Like they did two seasons ago, Liverpool win 2-0 at Portman Road.

McAteer shoots from range but there is not enough power to trouble Alisson, who makes the save down to his right.

Clarke’s shot from just outside the Liverpool penalty area takes a deflection off his teammate Diop and goes wide.

Davis and Ipswich can count themselves very, very lucky. It would have been a penalty but Szoboszlai was offside when the original ball was played. For the second time tonight, an offside call massively goes in Ipswich’s favour; one to deny Isak a hat-trick and now to deny Liverpool a penalty. A massive let-off for Ipswich.

Barcola’s first few touches in a Liverpool shirt are pretty good down the left. He is playing in his most natural position of wide left, with Gakpo now down the middle and Szoboszlai on the right.

If trends are anything to go by, Bradley Barcola will be introduced in the next three or four minutes. Andoni Iraola likes to change things around the hour mark and if the Frenchman warms up anymore, he will nearly overheat.

Kerkez is the latest player into the book for a foul on Fatawu.

Fatawu receives it out on the right for Ipswich and cuts inside onto his preferred left foot before curling an effort towards the far post but it goes wide.

Szoboszlai’s outswinger finds a free Mac Allister at the front post but the Argentine’s header is straight at Scherpen. That was a good chance for Mac Allister.

We are back under way at Portman Road. No changes for either side at the break.

Perhaps if Liverpool were playing a team with a bit more savvy, the 2-0 scoreline they currently protect would have been in jeopardy. Ipswich have put some nice moves together and had half chances but not enough to really turn the screw. Andoni Iraola, certainly, has been unhappy at times and it is becoming a trademark to see him spin around from the technical area in disgust when a ball has been squandered. In the main, though, he can be satisfied with this opening 45 minutes. Liverpool should be winning from here.

The first half is brought to an end at Portman Road and Isak’s quickfire double early in the half gives Liverpool a 2-0 lead at the break.

Wirtz feeds a lovely pass into the left channel to pick out the run of Isak into the Ipswich box but Diop comes in with a crucial challenge.

A chance for Wirtz as the ball falls to the German on the edge of the Ipswich box but his shot is saved by Scherpen down to his left.

Enciso is the first Ipswich player into the book tonight for delaying a restart.

Szoboszlai, for the third time in the half, shoots from range. Again, the Hungarian gets plenty of power on it but fortunately for Scherpen it is straight at him.

Enciso turns neatly not far outside the Liverpool box and then shoots but slices the shot a fair way wide.

Tommy Elphick, a member of Andoni Iraola’s coaching staff, is booked for his protestations. Liverpool are not happy with some of the fouls being given against them and then some that are not given for them, including a clear foul from Emersonn on Van Dijk that was not penalised.

Isak has the ball in the Ipswich net for the third time tonight and thinks he has his hat-trick but the offside flag goes up. It comes from a stunning piece of play from Wirtz down Liverpool’s left, taking up a pocket of space and taking the ball on the turn beautifully. He then spots Isak in space at the far post and picks him out perfectly, with Isak slotting home. However, the offside flag is up and replays prove he was just offside. Could Isak have timed his run just fractionally better and still reached the cross? Probably but it was very close.

Mac Allister receives a pass from Wirtz and, from just outside the box, decides to shoot but his effort goes just over. Scherpen did appear to have it covered anyway.

A crucial intervention from Araujo. Enciso drives down Ipswich’s right after Fatawu’s header, with Mac Allister tracking back. From the right side of the Liverpool box, Enciso’s deflected cross comes towards Maeda at the far post but Araujo makes an important clearance.

Moments later, Davis again meets a Fatawu cross at the far post but his header is off target.

Fatawu’s dangerous cross from the right all the way to the back post finds Davis, who heads back across goal. Emersonn takes a touch with his chest on the edge of the six-yard box before shooting but Jacquet is on hand to make a crucial block. Ipswich though do have their first corner of the game.

Lukic clips it in and Alisson should punch away with ease. However, the ball comes off Gakpo and, very fortunately for Alisson, the ball gets trapped between his own legs and he can gather. Alisson will be a relieved man.

Szoboszlai sends another powerful shot from range towards the goal and forces Scherpen into another decent save. Ipswich are not helping themselves at times by just giving the ball away inside their own half.

Szoboszlai comes close to adding a third for Liverpool. Fatawu inexplicably gives the ball away inside his own half before Mac Allister plays it forward to Szoboszlai, who takes just one touch before firing towards goal. Scherpen gets down well to his right to make the save.

And there he is. You have been waiting 12 months to see the Alexander Isak of Newcastle play for Liverpool but here he is, a confident, instinctive-finishing menace. His first goal was marvellous, his second was a work of art, given the pass from Cody Gakpo, and what a position Liverpool have put themselves in to get their first win under Andoni Iraola. And, while we are at it, Gakpo has made both Liverpool’s goals: what on earth were they doing thinking of selling him to Manchester City?

Isak, on his last trip to Portman Road, scored a hat-trick for Newcastle here in a 4-0 win back in December 2024. He already has two goals to his name tonight inside the opening quarter of an hour.

Emersonn misses from close range for Ipswich but the offside flag goes up against Greaves. It was a bad miss from Emersonn but Greaves, who had delivered the cross for Emersonn, was offside.

The first booking of the game goes the way of Mac Allister, who is booked slightly harshly for a foul on Enciso.

Moments later, Ipswich have their first effort of the game but Fatawu curls over from the edge of the box.

Another fine goal from Isak and Liverpool lead 2-0 not even 10 minutes into this game. It is Gakpo who assists again with a superb pass with the outside of his right foot from halfway into the left channel to pick out the run in behind of Isak. The Swede cuts inside Greaves onto his right before then chopping back onto his left. He then coolly slots home past Scherpen and Liverpool have the dream start.

Liverpool take a deserved lead at Portman Road. Kerkez wins the ball back for Liverpool on halfway and the ball comes to Gakpo. The Dutchman drives forward and spots Isak in space to his right. Isak’s movement is very clever as he drifts off the defender into space. He takes a touch before smashing the ball past Scherpen at his near post. Should Scherpen have saved that? Possibly but Isak did hit that very hard. For the first time this season, Liverpool lead in a Premier League match.

Andoni Iraola wondered what might happen when he first sat down to talk with Bradley Barcola.

Here was one of the world’s best wingers, with his 13 major honours, 28 international caps and £123m price tag – a combination that could easily lead a man to view himself through the prism of a superstar: never mind what I can do for you, what can you do for me?

Liverpool’s due diligence on Barcola had all been positive – not least from the currently injured Hugo Ekitike, who had been a vocal advocate of his compatriot’s capabilities to the recruitment team – but Iraola wanted to gauge for himself exactly what the 24-year-old was going to offer.

We are about to find out the two starting XIs at Portman Road. Will Bradley Barcola start for Liverpool on his debut?

The third matchday of the new Premier League season kicks off at Portman Road as newly-promoted Ipswich host Liverpool.

Andoni Iraola has drawn his first two games in charge of Liverpool, both 2-2 stalemates against Newcastle and Nottingham Forest respectively. Liverpool secured a move for forward Bradley Barcola from PSG in the final few days on the window for a fee that could rise to £123m and the Frenchman is set to make his Liverpool debut tonight.

“We are very happy with Bradley,” Iraola said. “He was our priority; to sign a very good player in that position. He has come with the right mentality. I like that he wanted Liverpool a lot, he just wanted to come here. That is a good first sign. Being the player he is and the things he has won recently, he has come with the willingness to help us. I am very happy with him.

“He trained well with us, and if everything goes well in today’s [Thursday] training, he will definitely be available for tomorrow [tonight]. He has trained with us three times. He has not had minutes in pre-season but he has been training normally with the group. It is a decision we have to make. We have to consider that he has not had minutes in pre-season.”

Liverpool won both fixtures when Ipswich were last in the Premier League two seasons ago, including a 2-0 win on the opening weekend in Arne Slot’s first game in charge of Liverpool as they went on to win the Premier League that season.

Ipswich won their first home game on their return to the Premier League, beating Sunderland 2-1 on the opening weekend. However, they fell to a 5-2 defeat in their first away game at Manchester United. Over the course of the summer transfer window, Ipswich made a total of 14 signings and spent over £200m.

“What we can do is perform in a way that always gives us a real chance, which we have done so far,” Ipswich boss Gary O’Neil said. “We were in that game at Manchester United until a couple of moments took it away from us. We were in it, so that is what we need to do, we need to make sure that no matter who it is, whether it is Liverpool, Manchester United, Manchester City, when they come to Portman Road, we need to make sure we are right in the game to give ourselves opportunities. We will always be a threat; we have scored four goals in two games. That is really good for a promoted side. We look a goal threat, and we need to keep that going and that will be tested.”

Team news from Portman Road to follow shortly.

#1842. Chelsea make 'contact' to sign £25m Real Betis talent

By Saikat Mandal | 14 Nov 2026 20:12

Chelsea are reportedly in contact with Jose Antonio Morante to enquire about a potential move to Stamford Bridge in the upcoming transfer window.

The Blues have made a stuttering start to their 2026-27 campaign and currently sit fifth in the Premier League table, with 16 points from 10 matches.

Chelsea spent heavily during the summer and also sold several players to balance the books, but they have continued to show a strong willingness to recruit emerging talent.

With Xabi Alonso at the helm, the Blues are expected to be linked with a number of promising players from Spain, and it appears that Morante has caught their attention.

The 19-year-old right-winger is part of Manuel Pellegrini's first-team squad and recently found the net in Betis's 5-2 victory over Osasuna in October.

A product of the club's youth academy, Morante has made only two substitute appearances this season, accumulating just 13 minutes of La Liga action.

According to a report from ABC, Chelsea regard him as a highly promising talent and have been monitoring his progress closely for the past few years.

Following the conclusion of the Under-19 European Championship in the summer, Chelsea made contact with the player's representatives, but the winger ultimately committed his future to Betis.

The report claims that, although Chelsea did not submit a formal bid, they did make a serious offer for the youngster.

Chelsea already have Estevao, Geovany Quenda and Jamie Gittens among their wide attacking options, all of whom are under the age of 23, and Morante fits the club's profile of targeting young, emerging talent.

Betis have moved to secure his future with a new contract containing a €30m (£25m) release clause, a measure designed to fend off interest from Chelsea and other potential suitors.

Morante is expected to feature more prominently this season, and the prospect of him leaving Betis in January looks increasingly unlikely, despite Chelsea's continued interest.

#1841. Encouraging signs for Scotland under-21s as Spanish training camp ends in draw against experienced USA side

Scotland Under-21s rounded off their Spanish training camp with a 1-1 friendly draw against the United States Under-23 side at Pinatar Arena, as preparations for the upcoming European Championship qualifiers continued.

The Young Scots faced a stern test against an American outfit featuring six players with senior international experience and led by 87-cap former international Steven Cherundolo. The USA were using the fixture as an important step in their preparations for the 2028 Olympic Games in Los Angeles.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Tony Docherty's side went into the contest in confident mood following an impressive 4-0 victory over Ukraine earlier in the week, looking to carry that momentum into their final fixture of the year in Murcia.

Their opponents presented a different challenge, bringing greater physical presence and experience to the encounter. However, Scotland proved more than a match for the Stars and Stripes, with St Mirren's Eseosa Sule scoring an 85th-minute equaliser to secure a share of the spoils.

Hearts striker James Wilson, who bagged a double against Ukraine on Thursday, featured in the starting line-up once again, alongside captain Tyler Fletcher, midfielders Lennon Miller and Kyle Ure, Andrew Tod of Dunfermline and Aberdeen full-back Mitchel Frame.

The fixture provided Docherty with another valuable opportunity to assess his much-changed squad as he builds towards the start of next year's qualification campaign. Following a productive week in Spain, Scotland can take plenty of encouragement from two performances against contrasting opposition.

Reflecting on the benefits of the training camp, Docherty said: “We were delighted with the performance and the result in the game against Ukraine on Thursday. It is a credit to the players that they have been able to take on board so much information in such a short period of time.

“The game against the USA was another step up in quality for the group. They were taking on a more experienced side, but we wanted to challenge the players, and we wanted to see what they can do on and off the ball in different situations.”

#1840. Cardinale discusses MSE creation and evolution within Milan: “Helping write a new chapter”

With the news of the new company leading AC Milan, Gerry Cardinale has offered a few words about what it means for the project.

In recent minutes, RedBird have announced a new parent company for Milan, aptly named ‘Milan Sports & Entertainment’. It’s a project that aims to put all of the club’s investments under one umbrella, whilst also allowing further investment into the city.

The new stadium is believed to have played a big part in this decision, and the Rossoneri will hopefully benefit significantly from this move.

As MilanNews relays, Cardinale offered some words in the announcement about the creation of the company, what it means to the city and for Rossoneri fans, what it means for the club.

“Over the past 25 years, we have worked alongside rights holders in the sports and media sectors to create innovative businesses that have transformed their respective industries.

“This evolution is based on a deep respect for the intellectual property assets that underpin these businesses, a long-term partnership with rights holders, and the ambition to fully unlock the potential of these teams and leagues, both on and off the pitch.

“Milan Sports & Entertainment represents the culmination of this journey and the work we have carried out since we first invested in AC Milan four years ago. Becoming a club owner has given us an even deeper understanding of what creates long-term value: winning, serving fans, and investing in the communities that give these institutions meaning.

“Today, we apply this experience on a different scale: not just to a single club, a single sport, or a single facility, but to an entire city and a portfolio that spans sports, lifestyle, and entertainment. I have known Brett Yormark and worked with him for 25 years.

“We’ve been working with Milan for years, and I can’t imagine a better executive in the international sports industry to help execute this strategy. Thanks to Brett, we can bring the best of American sports and live entertainment to Milan, helping write a new chapter in the city’s growth and international success.

“With AC Milan as our cornerstone, which will always be the driving force behind all our initiatives, we intend to build a world-class sports and entertainment platform capable of shaping the future of Milan and European sports, and bringing it back to the forefront of the global stage.”

Considering how much attention Cardinale has paid to the future of the Diavolo, and taking them back to the top level, it’s nice to hear it referenced once again in his latest statement. Hopefully this move is another step towards that.

#1838. Steyning’s second-half storm sinks Hastings United

The Barrowmen travelled full of confidence following their 2–1 home win over Horley Town. Hastings, meanwhile, were looking to respond after just one win in their previous four games, although a strong start to the league campaign meant they remained in the top three.

A crowd of 1,034 watched on a cold Saturday afternoon as an evenly contested opening offered few clear-cut chances.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Hastings broke the deadlock in the 20th minute when a corner caused chaos in the Steyning penalty area, with the ball going in off Conrad Honore for an own goal.

Chances remained scarce for the rest of the half as both sides defended well, allowing the hosts to take a slender advantage into the interval.

Steyning came flying out of the blocks after the restart and needed just four minutes to draw level, with Alex Brewer powering home a superb header.

Brewer struck again only a couple of minutes later, finishing off a fine Barrowmen counter-attack to turn the match on its head and put the visitors 2–1 ahead.

Charlie Pitcher extended Steyning’s lead on the hour mark, latching on to a well-judged headed flick-on to make it 3–1 and give the Barrowmen a two-goal cushion.

There was also an away debut from the bench for new signing Tosin Dada, whose arrival from Billingshurst had been announced late on Friday night.

Hastings threatened to pull a goal back, but Steyning goalkeeper Alfie Mansell produced a superb save, diving to his left.

Jesse Sentamu then rounded off an outstanding second-half display in the 90th minute, slotting past Harry Haines to make it 4–1 and ensure the Barrowmen headed home with all three points.

The victory lifts Steyning to 13th in the league table, while Hastings drop to fourth.

Both sides return to league action on Saturday – Steyning host Punjab while Hastings travel to Broadbridge Heath.

#1836. Who is Mario Frick? The new manager at Aberdeen who scored at Hampden, lost to Hibs and develops players

Mario Frick says he will create an environment at Aberdeen “where his players can thrive” after being appointed the next manager of the Pittodrie outfit.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The Dons hierarchy have moved quickly to land his successor and after a week of interviews have settled on former Liechtenstein striker Frick, 52, who has been out of work since the summer after end a five-year spell in Switzerland with Luzern.

Frick has also managed FC Balzers and FC Vaduz in his homeland. He will be assisted by Roman Matter, a 44-year-old Swiss coach who was also at Luzern. The pair are due to arrive in Aberdeen imminently ahead of Saturday’s league match against bottom club Kilmarnock.

“I'm excited to be joining Aberdeen FC,” said Frick. “It's a club with a proud history, passionate supporters and big ambitions.

“Together with the staff, my aim is to create an environment where the players can thrive, develop and perform at their very best, while working towards our goals as a team.”

Chief executive Adrian Bevington revealed Frick was the “unanimous” choice of the Aberdeen board after going through a robust process to identify him.

“We are delighted to welcome Mario Frick and his assistant coach Roman Matter to Aberdeen Football Club,” said Bevington. “This appointment follows a thorough and extensive recruitment process led by [sporting director] Lutz Pfannenstiel and myself on behalf of the board, during which we spoke to a number of highly qualified candidates.

“Mario has significant experience as a head coach and has delivered impressive results with both Vaduz and Luzern. He has a proven track record of building competitive teams and developing young players.

“Throughout our discussions, he demonstrated a clear vision, strong leadership qualities and a deep understanding of what is required to build a successful team.

“He was also exceptionally well regarded by the many people across the game we consulted during the process, and the Board was unanimous in its belief that he is the right person to lead Aberdeen Football Club forward.

“I would like to thank the board, in particular Willie Garner, and colleagues across the club for their diligence and support throughout this process.”

Pfannenstiel tipped Frick to have a “real impact at Pittodrie” and said his character will be crucial as the Dons look to climb the league table.

“I’m really pleased that we have been able to bring Mario Frick to Aberdeen,” said Pfannenstiel. “I have enormous respect for his football knowledge, leadership qualities and passion for the game.

“Mario is a strong personality with clear ideas about how he wants his teams to play. He brings energy, ambition and a winning mentality, and knows how to build a strong team environment.

“We were looking for the right person to lead the next chapter of Aberdeen FC, and I’m convinced Mario has the qualities, character and vision to make a real impact. I’m looking forward to working closely with him.”

Born in the Swiss town of Chur, Frick carved out a playing career as a physical striker and holds the record number of caps for Liechtenstein, scoring 16 goals in 125 appearances. One of those strikes came at Hampden in a 2-1 defeat by Scotland in 2010.

Also deployed as a centre-half, Frick played for clubs such as FC Basel, FC Zürich, St. Gallen, Grasshopper, Siena and Ternana before hanging up his boots in 2016 and moving into coaching.

At Vaduz, he secured promotion to the Swiss Super League, which earned him a move to Luzern. He spent five years with them, landing a fourth-placed finish. He faced Hibs in the 2024 Conference League, losing 5-3 on aggregate.

Frick most used formation with Vaduz and Luzern was a 4-4-2 diamond and he has carved out a reputation as a head coach who has developed younger players, most notably AC Milan and Switzerland midfielder Ardon Jashari.

#1834. Spain vs. England: Thomas Tuchel confirms one change and two boosts for Nations League finale

By Ben Knapton | 14 Nov 2026 20:34

England manager Thomas Tuchel has confirmed that James Trafford will start in goal for Sunday's UEFA Nations League group-stage finale against Spain.

The Three Lions take on the world champions at the Metropolitano Stadium in Madrid, knowing that only a win will do if they are to progress to the quarter-finals as group winners.

Tuchel's side have already sealed a last-eight spot with 12 points on the board, but La Roja boast a perfect total of 15, having bested England 3-2 at Wembley back in September.

England confirmed a top-two finish by edging out Croatia 2-1 on Thursday, on an evening when Jordan Pickford was selected to make his 94th senior international appearance.

However, the Everton shot-stopper will now make way for Leeds United's Trafford, as confirmed by Tuchel in his pre-game press conference on Saturday evening.

"James Trafford will play tomorrow. We want to see how far Traff is," Tuchel told the media, as Trafford gears up to win just his fifth cap for England since making his debut in March.

An unused substitute throughout the World Cup, Trafford started both of England's first two Nations League games in the current cycle, shipping three to Spain before keeping a clean sheet in a 2-0 win over the Czech Republic.

Both Trafford and Pickford have played every minute of the 2026-27 Premier League season so far, and both have four clean sheets to their name from their 10 appearances.

Pickford has conceded 10 goals to Trafford's eight, though, and the Leeds number one also boasts the best save percentage in the league, stopping 82.2% of the shots on target he has faced.

Arsenal's David Raya is second on the list with 80%, while Pickford lies sixth with a 73.7% save percentage, and the Everton man has also made fewer saves in total; 28 to Trafford's 37.

In addition, the former Manchester City goalkeeper has prevented 4.4 goals in the 2026-27 Premier League - the joint-most with Bart Verbruggen and Lukas Hornicek - strengthening his case to oust Pickford as England's number one.

As well as confirming that Trafford will start in between the sticks, Tuchel also revealed that Ezri Konsa and Djed Spence are both fit to play on Sunday.

The Arsenal centre-back and Inter Milan full-back were absent from Thursday's win over Croatia, having been restricted to individual training during the week as a precautionary measure.

However, Konsa and Spence's returns means that Tuchel will be blessed with a triple boost on Sunday, as Myles Lewis-Skelly is also back from a yellow-card suspension.

#1832. ‘With the times’ Scotland boss won me over with surprise call - here’s why he’s different to Steve Clarke

Scotland striker Che Adams admits he was instantly won over by head coach Sebastien Pocognoli after a surprise FaceTime call from the Belgian when he was out injured last month.

Adams, 30, was ruled out of Pocognoli’s inaugural camp in October after picking up a thigh injury with club side Torino, but was restored to the Scotland starting XI for their 2-1 win over North Macedonia on Friday night, and registered an assist for the first of John McGinn’s two goals.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

After being regular for former manager Steve Clarke during his seven year reign, Adams admits Scotland’s early performances under their new 38-year-old manager have been patchy so far. Still ironing out the teething issues often faced by teams in transition, he concedes they are yet to click, but says the squad believe in Pocognoli and his new methods.

Get our daily football newsletter by clicking here.

“The camps haven’t changed much but the manager is definitely more intense,” said Adams. “I think it’s the European style of play and thinking. It’s going to take time for him to understand the boys, understand us as players and understand us as a squad. This gaffer has good ideas, a good approach to the game. Everyone’s buying into it and I definitely think we’ll see the benefits.

“With Steve [Clarke] you could have a laugh and you can do that with this gaffer as well, but he’s a lot more intense in terms of detail, off the pitch telling you where to be and what to do. In the last camp when I was out injured he was on asking how my injury was, how long I’d be out for and if I still wanted to be part of it.

“Coming off a transitional period like we have just now, it’s difficult to know where you are and what you want to do. But all the boys here want to play for our country and do Scotland proud. I had no doubts about it, it’s good to get away from Italy for a while, be around some good lads.”

Striking trio Kieron Bowie, Oli McBurnie and Robbie Ure were all called into the squad by Pocognoli for last month’s Nations League games against Slovenia, North Macedonia and Switzerland, with Adams injured and Lyndon Dykes and George Hirst both left out.

With enhanced competition for a starting spot, the Torino hitman said the Belgian ensured he kept in contact with him during his injury layoff, revealing the unique method Pocognoli implemented with the team since he was appointed manager in August.

“I heard from the manager the last time when I wasn’t in the camp,” said Adams. “He loves a FaceTime call. I think he’s taken a few of the boys by surprise when they’ve been out walking their dogs and stuff. I think KT [Kieran Tierney] was out for a walk when he phoned him. He just calls out of the blue and has done it to a few of the boys. It’s unexpected and it’s different because we’ve never experienced something like that, but it’s good.

“The manager is with the times, really, he’s brought in his new ideas. He’s a few years younger and has a different philosophy on how he wants his team to play. It just takes time to click but it’s up to us as players now to show we can do what he wants. We have been together for a number of years now so we know each other’s game. You could see on Friday us starting to put the manager’s things in practice, we won a lot of balls high with our pressing.

“For me, it’s a bit different to what I’m used to at club level because that’s a little bit more free. I can roam where I want in and around the back line for my club, but I am enjoying it. When you’re playing with boys like John McGinn and Scott McTominay who have the creativity, that eye for goal and pass forward that you don’t really get at club level it is good.

“The gaffer wanted me to run deep on Friday as well, so nothing changed there. As games go on, stretching the opposition helps John and Scott get on the ball where they can hurt teams with their creativity. You can definitely see things are coming together, you could see how we were building up and playing out. You have to credit the manager for putting the belief in the young players who have come in as well.”

France, who sit second in their Nations League Group A behind Italy, will now play Turkey in their final group game on Sunday night.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

But despite the scoreline against Italy, Zidane has urged his players not to panic.

‘There were some good things, especially in the first half where we should have focused on what we did well. After that, we did some less good things,’ Zidane told TF1.

‘We lost the match, so naturally there were some more complicated situations, particularly in duels and one-on-one situations, we weren’t quite as good. It’s all part of the learning process.

‘When we were in difficulty, we didn’t know how to react and stay within the game plan we had put in place. We did it in the first half, but when they took the lead, we became a little scattered, especially defensively.

‘Tonight wasn’t a bad game. There’s room for improvement. I told the players we shouldn’t panic. We became more fragile as the match went on. What I told them is that it was a defeat, but not entirely deserved.

‘We did some good things and some not-so-good things. We’ll analyse it when we’re in Bordeaux to prepare for our match. We just need to rest and focus on the game we have left.’
